grants.Description: OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF AUGUST 31 – SEPTEMBER 4, 2026
grants.Chemicals and Industrial Feedstocks:
DOE ASPECT (DE-FOA-0003647), $58,000,000 across roughly 10 awards, $2,000,000–$20,000,000, cost share required. Four subtopics spanning bench-scale R&D through design, construction, and operation of integrated pre-pilot facilities producing chemicals from alternative and waste feedstocks.

Required concept paper due October 9, 2026; full application December 1. No concept paper, no full application.
grants.Space Technology / Photovoltaics: DOE Integrated Energy Systems Office FY2026 Space Photovoltaic R&D Program, administered through TechWerx, up to $12,000,000 across 7–11 awards — up to $1.5M each in Topic 1 (PARSECS) and up to $2M each in Topic 2 (Manufacturing R&D). Universities, nonprofits, and for-profits are all eligible as lead applicants. Due October 8, 2026.
grants.NASA: SSERVI CAN-5 (NNH26ZDA016C) Step-1 proposals are due September 29, 2026 — up to $9M in total funding for the first year; up to $1.8M/year; 5 awards anticipated; Step-2 December 4, 2026.

Museums for America is the largest at $21,699,000 across roughly 122 awards; National Leadership Grants for Libraries follows at $11,500,000. Eligibility varies per grant but is generally libraries and museums.

Pre-applications due November 2, 2026; full proposals by invitation only.
grants.Natural Resources / Coastal: NOAA DARRP Restoration Implementation Grants (NOAA-NMFS-HCPO-2026-33781), $2,500,000–$100,000,000 per award, no match. Institutions of higher education, nonprofits, and for-profits only; federal, state, and tribal governments are excluded because of their trustee role. Due November 18, 2026.
grants.California State Opportunities:
CEC GFO-26-301 Characterizing Non-Driving Electric Vehicle Energy Efficiency — EPIC 4 applied research and development. $1.5M in total funding; $1M-$1.5M per award. Due October 28, 2026; questions due September 23; pre-application workshop September 16.

State Parks Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program (SPP) Round 5, Proposition 4 — $188,500,000, $200,000–$8,500,000 per award, no match required, due December 17, 2026. Cities, counties, districts, JPAs, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits.

California Employment Development Department — Farmworkers Advancement Program (FAP) Grant, Program Year 2026–27, $10M in total funding; up to $1M per award. NOI due Sept. 25, 2026; applications due Oct. 12, 2026.

CEC GFO-26-401, Equitable Building Decarbonization Tribal Direct Install Program — Application for Tribes. grants.Energy / Subsurface:
DOE Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office Request for Information (DE-FOA-0003671), gauging investor and financial-sector interest in developing and commercializing subsurface energy technologies across coal, oil and gas, and geothermal. Responses due October 5, 2026.

This is an RFI, not a NOFO — no funding is attached and DOE is not accepting applications. Value here is positioning and relationship-building, not a submission.

CDFA OARS Proposition 4 Regional Farm Equipment Sharing Pilot Program — public listening sessions September 2–8, 2026; draft guidelines for comment Winter 2026; solicitation anticipated Spring 2027.

California Avocado Commission Fall 2026 Research Program — pre-proposals due September 30, 2026.

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Energy — Accelerating Scale-up and Pre-piloting of Emerging Chemical Technologies (ASPECT)
grants.Opportunity #: DE-FOA-0003647; Assistance Listing 81.087 (Renewable Energy Research and Development). Grants.gov opportunity 363815. Issued following Notice of Intent DE-FOA-0003646.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Critical Minerals and Emerging Innovations (CMEI), through its AFFO, administered by the Golden Field Office. NOFO questions to ASPECT@doe.gov.
grants.Award Range: $2,000,000 minimum to $20,000,000 maximum — a wide spread, reflecting the four subtopics spanning bench-scale R&D through integrated pre-pilot construction.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Broadly open: state, county, city or township, special district, and federally recognized tribal governments; public and Indian housing authorities; for-profits including small businesses; nonprofits with and without 501(c)(3) status; other Native American tribal organizations; public, state, and private institutions of higher education; independent school districts; and individuals.

Participation limits are the thing to read carefully here. Because DOE's stated goal is moving technologies quickly to market, several entity types are capped at the subrecipient level:

• Institutions of higher education may be recipient or subrecipient for Topic Area 1, but subrecipient only for Topic Area 2.

• DOE FFRDCs may apply as subrecipients only — not as prime recipients — and only where there is no conflict of interest. Non-DOE FFRDCs are likewise subrecipient-only.

• The National Energy Technology Laboratory may participate as a subrecipient, not as prime.

• Federal agencies and instrumentalities other than DOE may participate as subrecipients only.
grants.Deadline: Concept Paper is required and due October 9, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET. Full Application due December 1, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET.
grants.Program Focus:
Research, development, and pre-pilot testing of technologies that produce chemicals from alternative and waste feedstocks, with the aim of mobilizing domestic alternative feedstock resources. Two topic areas, each with two subtopics offering different on-ramps by technology maturity.

Topic Area 1 — R&D phase. Subtopic 1a advances early-stage research to bench scale. Subtopic 1b moves projects closer to pre-pilot scale, to the point where critical unit operations must be further developed and demonstrated.

Topic Area 2 — pre-pilot scale and operations. Both subtopics aim at integrated pre-pilot systems that are actually operated. Subtopic 2a targets preliminary pre-pilot testing of critical unit operations before full-system engineering and design can begin; Subtopic 2b covers technologies ready for design and construction of an integrated pre-pilot facility.

A Teaming Partner List (TPL-0000073) was compiled under the NOI to encourage collaboration and new team formation — useful for a client that needs a feedstock, offtake, or engineering partner. The full NOFO is on eere-exchange.energy.gov.
grants.Primary Sector: Chemical Manufacturing; Alternative and Waste Feedstocks; Bench-to-Pilot Scale-Up; Process Engineering; Critical Minerals and Emerging Innovations; Industrial Decarbonization
grants.Link to NOFO: ASPECT on Simpler.Grants.gov; EERE eXCHANGE (full NOFO, search DE-FOA-0003647); Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Energy, Integrated Energy Systems Office — FY2026 Space Photovoltaic (PV) Research and Development Program
grants.Opportunity #: No Grants.gov or SAM.gov opportunity number. Administered for DOE by RTI International through the TechWerx platform and identified there as the FY2026 Space Photovoltaic (PV) Research and Development (R&D) Program.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Integrated Energy Systems Office (IESO), which consolidates the former wind, solar, and grid integration programs. Administered by RTI International (TechWerx).
grants.Total Funding: Up to $12,000,000 total: $8,000,000 anticipated for Topic 1 and $4,000,000 for Topic 2.
grants.Award Range:
Topic 1 (PARSECS): 5–9 awards of up to $1,500,000 each. Topic 2 (Space PV Manufacturing R&D): 2–3 awards of up to $2,000,000 each. Projects of three years or less.

The summary language states up to 9 awards in Topic 1 and up to 3 in Topic 2; the objective section describes 7–11 awards overall.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Institutions of higher education, nonprofit entities, and for-profit entities may serve as lead participants.

Applicant must qualify as a domestic entity.
grants.Deadline:
October 8, 2026, 11:59 PM Eastern, through the TechWerx application portal.

Informational webinar September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET. Office hours September 29 and October 6, 2026 at 3:00 PM ET. DOE selection expected December 2026; negotiations run roughly two months after selection.
grants.Program Focus:
Durable, high-power space photovoltaic technologies that can be manufactured at high volume and low cost. A June 2026 IESO workshop concluded that no single U.S. space PV technology currently combines high performance, long-term durability, and scalable low-cost manufacturing.

Five areas of interest: (A) III-V PV — substrate re-use targeting at least 27% PCE with >95% yield after five wafer re-uses, low-cost metallization, and reduced gallium and germanium dependence; (B) crystalline silicon — radiation-hardened cells retaining ≥80% of beginning-of-life maximum power over 10-year deployments, and thin-wafer cells targeting 23% PCE at AM0; (C) perovskite — degradation mitigation under space stressors, new multijunction designs, and combined accelerated stress testing; (D) other PV technologies meeting the same criteria; and (E) low-cost space PV testing — rapid in-orbit test platforms with in-situ characterization, and ground-based combined AST equipment.

Topic 1 funds early-stage research-cell work (~1″ substrate) on a 5–10 year horizon. Topic 2 funds coupon-scale prototypes (~20–100 cm²) that are 2–3 years from deployment readiness.
grants.Primary Sector: Space Photovoltaics; III-V and Perovskite Multijunction Cells; Radiation-Hardened Silicon; Critical Minerals Supply Chain (gallium, germanium); Accelerated Stress Testing; Space Economy Manufacturing
grants.Link to Solicitation: FY2026 Space PV R&D on TechWerx; Project Narrative Template (DOCX); Summary Slide Template (PPTX); TechWerx opportunities index

grants.Description: NASA — Solar System Exploration Research Virtual Institute Cooperative Agreement Notice-5 (SSERVI CAN-5)
grants.Agency / Funder: NASA Headquarters — Science Mission Directorate and Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, jointly.
grants.Total Funding: $9M for the first year of all new awards
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Proposers must be affiliated with an institution registered at NSPIRES. NASA generally funds only U.S. institutions; non-U.S. organizations may participate on a no-exchange-of-funds basis under the NASA Grant and Cooperative Agreement Manual.

Proposals must be multi-institutional and team-based. • Government Organizations o Federal government agencies o State governments o County governments o City or township governments • Special district governments o Native American tribal governments (federally recognized) o Native American tribal governments (other than federally recognized) • Education Organizations o Independent school districts o Public and state-controlled institutions of higher education o Private institutions of higher education 6 • Nonprofit Organizations o Nonprofits having a 501(c)(3) status with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), other than institutions of higher education o Nonprofits that do not have a 501(c)(3) status with the IRS, other than institutions of higher education • For-Profit Organizations o Organizations other than small businesses • Small Businesses o Small business grants may be awarded to companies meeting the size standards established by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) for most industries in the economy
grants.Deadline:
Step-1 proposals due September 29, 2026. Step-2 (full) proposals due December 4, 2026.

Only proposers who submit a Step-1 are eligible to submit a Step-2. Submission is through NSPIRES only — the CAN is synopsized on Grants.gov but applications cannot be filed there. Clarification questions are due no later than 14 calendar days before the Step-2 date, to HQ-SSERVI@mail.nasa.gov.
grants.Program Focus:
Research fundamental to understanding the Moon and its near-space environment, to enable future human lunar exploration under Artemis. “Mars forward” proposals that use lunar-focused research to develop approaches to Mars exploration are also welcome.

NASA states that proposals complementing current CAN-4 institute teams, or addressing research areas not currently covered by the institute, will be given strong consideration.
grants.Primary Sector: Lunar and Planetary Science; Artemis Human Exploration; In-Situ Resource Utilization; Space Environment Research; Multi-Institutional Research Institutes
grants.Link to NOFO: SSERVI CAN-5 on Simpler.Grants.gov; Full CAN text on NSPIRES; Grants.gov listing; Current SSERVI teams

grants.Description: Institute of Museum and Library Services — Museums for America (FY2027)
grants.Opportunity #: 21MP-FY27; Assistance Listing 45.032 (21st Century Museum Professional Program). Grants.gov opportunity 363769.
grants.Agency / Funder: Institute of Museum and Library Services. Program contact imls-museumgrants@imls.gov.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Eligibility is restricted to organizations that are:

• Located in the United States or any U.S. Territories or Freely Associated States; AND

• A unit of a State, local or Tribal government or a private, nonprofit organization; AND

• A museum, an organization or association related to the museum field, an institution of higher education.
grants.Program Focus: Projects that build career pathways, strengthen professional networks, and identify and share effective workforce education and training practices in the museum field. Note the $100,000 floor — the highest minimum in the FY2027 slate, and the smallest program by total funding.
grants.Primary Sector: Museum Workforce Development; Career Pathways; Professional Networks; Training Practice Research

grants.Description: USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture — Emergency Citrus Disease Research and Extension (ECDRE) Pre-Applications
grants.Opportunity #: USDA-NIFA-SCRI-012018; Assistance Listing 10.309 (Specialty Crop Research Initiative). Grants.gov opportunity 363785. Mandatory funding category.
grants.Agency / Funder: USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture. Application questions to grantapplicationquestions@usda.gov, Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Central.
grants.Award Range: $500,000 minimum to $15,000,000 maximum. Per UC ANR's summary of the NOFO: Standard Projects up to $1.5M over 24–36 months; Coordinated Agricultural Projects up to $15M over 36–60 months.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Federal agencies, national laboratories, colleges and universities, research institutions and organizations, private organizations or corporations, State Agricultural Experiment Stations, the Cooperative Extension Service, individuals, or groups of two or more of these.

Duplicate or multiple submissions with the same lead PD are not allowed and will disqualify both applications. An applicant may be Co-PD on multiple submissions while submitting one unique application as lead PD in the same fiscal year. USDA will not accept applications for dangerous gain-of-function research as defined in Section 8 of E.O. 14292.
grants.Deadline: Pre-applications due November 2, 2026, 5:00 p.m. Eastern, via Grants.gov. Full proposals are by invitation only.
grants.Program Focus:
Tactics and strategies to control Huanglongbing and its disease complex for financially sustainable U.S. citrus production. All funded projects must integrate research and Extension and deliver solutions growers can deploy in the near term.

Priorities in stated order of importance: HLB-resistant or tolerant commercial varieties; regional management or eradication of the Asian citrus psyllid; improved ACP and HLB detection and surveillance; treatments for infected trees and strategies to maintain productivity; delivery systems for therapeutics and nutrition; screening and prioritization of intervention targets; a reliable method for culturing Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus; understanding of the HLB–vector–citrus pathosystem; and understanding of citrus production ecology and the HLB–ACP disease complex.

The pre-application is a three-page, 1.5-spaced Stakeholder Relevance Statement covering project type, funding request, industry significance, deliverables, stakeholder involvement, approach, and team experience. Invited applicants submit full proposals using the same project objectives.
grants.Primary Sector: Citrus Production; Huanglongbing and Asian Citrus Psyllid Management; Plant Pathology; Integrated Research and Extension; Specialty Crop Research
grants.Link to NOFO: ECDRE on Simpler.Grants.gov; FY26 ECDRE Pre-Application NOFO (PDF); NIFA ECDRE program page; UC ANR summary

grants.Description: NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service — DARRP Restoration Implementation Grants (2026)
grants.Opportunity #: NOAA-NMFS-HCPO-2026-33781; Assistance Listing 11.463 (Habitat Conservation). Grants.gov opportunity 363758.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Commerce — NOAA, National Marine Fisheries Service, Damage Assessment, Remediation and Restoration Program. Program contact David Landsman.
grants.Total Funding: Funding is expected to be provided on an as-available basis to maintain the initial cooperative agreement for up to five years, and is dependent upon the level of funding made available by trustee councils and NOAA. Total anticipated funding for initial cooperative agreements under this competition is up to $100 million. NOAA anticipates that a typical, awarded cooperative agreement will range from $2.5 million to $50 million. NOAA does not anticipate accepting proposals under this solicitation with a first-year budget less than $500,000 or more than $20 million, and with a total five-year budget less than $2.5 million or more than $100 million..
grants.Award Range: $2,500,000 minimum to $100,000,000 maximum. Number of awards not published.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Institutions of higher education, nonprofits, and commercial (for-profit) organizations only.

Applications from federal, state, or tribal governments will not be considered because of their potential role as trustee council members. Local government applications will be considered only if they identify potential large-scale restoration opportunities based on current or anticipated restoration plans. Applications from individuals or federal employees will not be considered. NOAA encourages ineligible organizations to work with eligible applicants.
grants.Program Focus:
Collaboration with non-federal partners to implement marine and coastal habitat restoration and conservation tied to oil spills, hazardous substance releases, and other natural resource damages. Activities are authorized under the Oil Pollution Act, CERCLA, the Clean Water Act, the National Marine Sanctuaries Act, and other authorities including the RESTORE Act.

NOAA is looking for partners capable of implementing across a wide geographic scale. Recipients implement activities identified in consent decrees or natural resource damage assessment and restoration plans, and may develop or solicit projects to meet restoration goals — including collaborating with trustees to select activities for contract or subaward, managing competitions to subaward projects, and conducting pre- and post-restoration evaluation and monitoring. Restoration planning and technique development, such as environmental compliance analyses or planning for potential future incidents, are also in scope.

Stated outcomes include rebuilding productive and sustainable fisheries, contributing to recovery of threatened and endangered species, and improving economic vitality including local employment.
grants.Primary Sector: Coastal and Marine Habitat Restoration; Natural Resource Damage Assessment; Oil Spill and Hazardous Substance Response; Fisheries Recovery; Endangered Species Conservation; RESTORE Act

grants.Description: California Energy Commission — GFO-26-301: Characterizing Non-Driving Electric Vehicle Energy Efficiency
grants.Opportunity #: California Grants Portal ID 190281. Solicitation for Proposals (SFP) issued by EDD; no separate departmental grant number published. Status Active.
grants.Agency / Funder: California Employment Development Department, in coordination with the Labor and Workforce Development Agency. Program contact Brandon Raveling, (916) 891-9189, brandon.raveling@edd.ca.gov.
grants.Total Funding: $10,000,000 from WIOA Governor's Discretionary Funds. Note that although this is administered as a California state solicitation, the underlying money is federal.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Eligible applicants include:

· Non-profit organizations

· Local labor partners

· Tribal governments

· Community colleges

· Local workforce boards

· Education and training providers

· Farmworker serving organizations

Geography. Two target regions: Region 1 serves farmworkers in San Joaquin Valley or Northern California counties; Region 2 serves Coastal or Southern California counties. Applicants may serve any region or county if the need is supported in the proposal, but preference goes to applicants serving counties within the identified regions.
grants.Deadline:
Proposals due October 12, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Pacific.

Informational webinar September 15, 2026, 10:00 a.m. PT. Pre-registration is required for all attendees through the link in the SFP by 9:00 a.m. PT on September 15 — registration closes one hour before the webinar starts. Notice of Intent to apply by September 25, 2026, noon PT to WSBSFP3@edd.ca.gov. The Portal's “Letter of Intent Required” field says No, so the NOI is encouraged rather than mandatory — but it is free, and worth filing for any client considering this.

SFP release was moved up to September 3, 2026 per the Portal's change notes. Expected award announcement January 31, 2027; period of performance February 1, 2027 through March 31, 2029.
grants.Program Focus:
Regional projects delivering essential-skills and upskilling training that position farmworkers either to advance within the agricultural industry or to prepare for advancement outside it. EDD frames the program as addressing existing and emerging gaps in the current workforce system for farmworkers.

Funded programs are expected to move participants toward good-quality jobs — family-sustaining wages, benefits, predictable hours, career advancement, and worker voice — and to provide wrap-around support that prevents job loss and builds a foundation for upward mobility, including referrals to health, housing, and educational resources and career and financial coaching.

This builds on prior Farmworkers Advancement Program rounds, so an applicant with documented outcomes from an earlier FAP or comparable workforce grant is well positioned.
grants.Funding Instrument: Subcontract with EDD, reimbursement basis. After award, EDD contacts subrecipients to finalize subcontract details and may request changes to the original project proposal before exhibits are finalized. Payment is tied to the services and participant counts stated in the executed subcontract.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Applicants must demonstrate the ability to leverage at least 20 percent of their budget with resources from other sources. EDD encourages leveraging human capital and other resources to maximize project success. Treat this as a 20% leverage requirement for planning purposes and confirm the allowable forms of leverage in the SFP.
grants.Primary Sector: Farmworker Workforce Development; Agricultural Labor; Essential Skills and Upskilling Training; WIOA Governor's Discretionary Funds; Wrap-Around Services; Disadvantaged Communities
grants.Link to Solicitation: FAP PY 26-27 on the California Grants Portal; EDD Workforce Development Solicitations for Proposals page; EDD home

grants.Description: California Energy Commission — GFO-26-401: Equitable Building Decarbonization Tribal Direct Install Program, Application for Tribes
grants.Opportunity #: GFO-26-401. Grant Funding Opportunity; status Active. Reliability, Renewable Energy & Decarbonization Incentives Division, Equitable Building Decarbonization Program.
grants.Agency / Funder: California Energy Commission. Program contact equitablebuildingdecarb@energy.ca.gov. Authorized by AB 209 (Committee on Budget, Ch. 251, Stats. 2022); Tribal Direct Install Program Guidelines adopted January 2026.
grants.Total Funding: Up to $30,000,000 is available under this solicitation.5 This includes grant awards to implementing tribes and funds allocated to nonimplementing tribes. Nonimplementing tribes will not receive grant awards; rather, funds allocated to nonimplementing tribes will be granted to the program implementer, selected through a separate competitive solicitation, who will perform decarbonization retrofits and provide related services for nonimplementing tribes. CEC expects to release a separate competitive solicitation in 2026 for a program implementer which will be funded with a portion of the program’s $30,000,000 allocation.
grants.Award Range: $75K base allocation for each applicant plus:
grants.Eligible Applicants:
California Native American tribes and tribal organizations. This solicitation is the “Application for Tribes” track of the program.

Building eligibility is the operative screen. Eligible buildings must be residential buildings in California built before January 1, 2020, and must be owned or managed by California Native American tribes or tribal organizations, or owned by enrolled members of California Native American tribes.

Buildings are not required to be located on tribal lands to be eligible — per the CEC program page, which materially widens the pool of qualifying housing.

Confirm applicant-entity requirements and any Group 1 / Group 2 distinctions against the Solicitation Manual.
grants.Deadline:
February 19, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Released September 4, 2026.

Questions deadline October 21, 2026, 5:00 p.m. Pre-application workshop October 7, 2026, 10:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m., remote access only.

Submission is through the new ECAMS portal. Applicants must have or create an ECAMS user account to apply. This is a change from prior CEC practice and account setup should not be left to the last week — CEC has posted User Registration Instructions and an Applying for a Solicitation guide.

Note the schedule slipped: CEC's program page had anticipated releasing the tribal application in Spring 2026.
grants.Program Focus:
Upgrading residential buildings with energy-efficient electric appliances, energy efficiency improvements, and related measures. Under the EBD Direct Install model these upgrades are installed at no cost to participating households.

Program goals are reducing greenhouse gas emissions from existing buildings and advancing energy equity, alongside lower energy bills, better indoor air quality, improved resilience to extreme heat, and local workforce development. CEC has run tribal listening sessions on this subprogram since May 2023, with draft guidelines and a public workshop in summer 2025 before January 2026 adoption.

A CEQA Compliance Form (Attachment 7) is part of the application package. The program guidelines were adopted under categorical exemptions (CEQA Guidelines §§ 15307, 15308 and 15061(b)(3)), but project-level compliance is still the applicant's to document.
grants.Funding Instrument: Competitive state grant, AB 209 Equitable Building Decarbonization Program funds.
grants.Primary Sector: Building Decarbonization; Tribal Housing; Residential Electrification and Weatherization; Energy Efficiency Retrofits; Energy Equity; Indoor Air Quality and Heat Resilience
grants.Link to Solicitation: GFO-26-401 on the CEC site; Solicitation Manual (DOCX); Pre-application workshop; EBD Tribal Direct Install program page; ECAMS portal

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Energy — Request for Information: Gauging Investor Interest in the Development and Commercialization of Subsurface Energy Technologies
grants.Opportunity #: DE-FOA-0003671; Assistance Listing 81.089 (Fossil Energy Research and Development). Grants.gov opportunity 363797.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office (HGEO), issued through the National Energy Technology Laboratory.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Unrestricted. DOE requests input from all stakeholders, and particularly from the financial sector.
grants.Deadline:
Responses due October 5, 2026.

Responses must be submitted electronically to DE-FOA-0003671@netl.doe.gov. Archive date November 4, 2026.
grants.Program Focus:
DOE is gauging investor interest in the development and commercialization of subsurface energy technologies, with the aim of connecting private capital and public-private partnership programs to industry opportunities. HGEO would contribute technical expertise across the Office of Subsurface Energy's three core program areas — coal, oil and gas, and geothermal — using its R&D capabilities to support industry and capital.

Client value here is positioning, not submission. A response places a client's technology and capital needs in front of HGEO ahead of any future solicitation shaped by this RFI. Worth flagging to any energy-technology client with a commercialization gap, and to investors in the portfolio.
grants.Primary Sector: Subsurface Energy; Geothermal; Oil and Gas; Coal; Technology Commercialization; Public-Private Partnership and Private Capital

grants.Description: CDFA Office of Agricultural Resilience and Sustainability — Proposition 4 Climate Bond Funding for Climate Smart Agriculture
grants.Opportunity #: No solicitation number. Surfaced through UC ANR Contracts & Grants Updates, September 2, 2026.
grants.Agency / Funder: California Avocado Commission (CAC) — private commodity commission, not a public funder.
grants.Total Funding: Not published as a program total.
grants.Award Range: No stated maximum. Current annual awards range from approximately $5,500 to $243,700, with a median of roughly $56,000.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Not restricted by organization type in the published summary. Preference goes to proposals addressing high-priority topics that have not previously received CAC funding.
grants.Deadline:
Pre-proposals due September 30, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Pacific.

Pre-proposals may not exceed five pages and must summarize the research priority addressed, project team, rationale, objectives, deliverables, methods, timeline, milestones, estimated budget, and relevant avocado research experience.
grants.Program Focus:
Cultural methods. Updated production cost studies; practices used by consistently high-yielding growers; leaching requirements for modern rootstocks and different water sources; nitrogen planning and nitrate credits; applications of soil-health research to avocado production.

Irrigation. Economic analysis of small-farm irrigation automation; practices or technologies to mitigate chloride impacts.

Pest research. Avocado lace bug management; fruit fly non-host data for GEM, Lamb Hass, and other varieties; an updated avocado thrips degree-day model.

Agricultural chemical research. Avocado thrips and persea mite management; resistance management for Phytophthora controls; chemical and cultural management of avocado branch canker.

The solicitation identifies additional topics of interest within each research area.
grants.Primary Sector: Avocado Production Research; Irrigation and Water Quality; Entomology and Pest Management; Plant Pathology; California Specialty Crops
grants.Link to Solicitation: California Avocado Commission Fall 2026 RFP (PDF); UC ANR Contracts & Grants Updates post

The Government may employ analytical and support tools, including spreadsheets, databases, document comparison software, search capabilities, and Government-approved artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, to assist evaluators with preliminary support tasks such as, but not limited to, organizing information, identifying references, summarizing proposal content, recognizing solicitation requirement compliance, identifying proposal strengths and weaknesses, highlighting proposal merits, identifying initial draft evaluation ratings, and preparing initial draft evaluation and selection documentation. Notwithstanding the use of support tools to assist the evaluation process, all final evaluation judgements, 20 including technical value, cost evaluation, the assignment or assessment of confidence ratings, best value determinations, and selection decisions, will be made exclusively by duly appointed Government personnel. The Government retains sole responsibility for all inherently governmental functions and will not delegate decision making authority to any support tool. The Government is committed to protecting all offeror proprietary and sensitive information; any analytical and support tool used will operate in a secure environment, consistent with all applicable data protection regulations, and will not transmit data to external systems.
